distance_note: Adjoins Mission Bay North, which lies across 4th Street and King Street from the yard. OCII's December 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map labels N5A, N6 and N7 in this area with no land-use color and no drawn boundary; whether the yard is inside or outside Mission Bay North's project area is not settled here (DataSF's project-area layer places part of it inside).
summary: A 20-acre active Caltrain rail yard and maintenance facility at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square, including the existing 4th & King Street Station itself. Owned by Prologis, with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. SF Planning is processing it as the "SF Railyards Planning Program" (Case No. 2023-000384CWP); Prologis has floated a development concept of up to 2,500 housing units and about 8 million square feet in total (about half commercial), anchored by a tower as tall as 850 feet (SF Standard, March 2026); a Development Agreement is the expected approval path, the same one used for Pier 70, Mission Rock and Potrero Power Station.

milestones.text: Prologis, Caltrain and the City of San Francisco start public outreach and engagement on the SF Railyards Planning Program (listed in the FAQ's expected milestones as 'Fall 2022').
SF Planning Commission informational presentation on the SF Railyards Planning Program (Case No. 2023-000384CWP); no action taken, informational only.

Prologis submits an application to the Planning Department for the site: up to 2,500 housing units and about 8 million square feet in total at buildout (about half commercial), anchored by an 850-foot tower at the site of the 4th & King station.

open_questions: Whether Prologis's March 2026 submission constitutes a formal Preliminary Project Assessment/application distinct from the January 2025 informational Case No. 2023-000384CWP, or is still pre-application, is not confirmed here -- SF Planning's project page and hearing calendar are the places to check.

No named individual or group's public position on this specific project (for or against) has been found and sourced yet, distinct from the SF Railyards Working Group's general, collectively-summarized 'conceptual support' described in the January 2025 staff report.

The site's geometry is bounded by real street centerlines on three sides; the fourth (where King St's real centerline data ends short of 7th St, at the I-280 interchange) is a straight closing line, not a surveyed street -- see the geometry file's own accuracy_caveat.

2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the SF Chronicle article (January 8, 2025) reports the 850-foot tower concept but says it is too early to say how many units; the 2,500-unit and 8-million-sq-ft figures come from the SF Standard (March 10, 2026). The project page does not itself state the Development Agreement path, the FAQ does. Three active Assessor parcels lie inside this site's polygon (see the geometry file); whether this should be a real-parcel record is unresolved.
